newsitem.title: CHINA: China data firm to expand information service.
newsitem.headline: China data firm to expand information service.

text.p: A financial data firm with investment from China's state-controlled Xinhua news agency will offer clients overseas financial information and data via satellite delivery, officials said on Monday.
The Xinhua Financial Information Consultancy Ltd will expand its service from May by adding overseas financial reports such as information on grain, edible oils and metals, a company official said.
An advertisement in the China Securities newspaper on Monday announced the successful trial operation of the company's satellite transmission.
"We have linked up with several overseas bourses," the official said, but added that the firm could not yet offer information on overseas futures trading.

The financial information consultancy firm was owned 45 percent by the Xinhua News Agency Centre, a division of the Xinhua News Agency, and the remaining 55 percent was held by a subsidiary of state-owned China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp.
Xinhua news agency has regulatory control over real-time economic information supply in China under a State Council, or cabinet, decree issued on January 16.

The decree requires foreign vendors supplying such information -- mainly Reuters Holdings Plc, Dow Jones Telerate and Bloomberg -- to apply for permission to market their services in China and to allow Xinhua to monitor their product.
